action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is solid, and this is the kind of phase in which spending to win new and returning users has historically paid back best, especially among active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price has spent six days just under its 50-day average and the Fed decides on 28 October, the sensible way to apply it is in steps: add spend gradually, review weekly, and speed up once price wins back about $81,842. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC is about 10% above its 200-day average ($73,028), which is still rising.
Up about 26% over 90 days; about 78% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But price ($80,252) has been under its 50-day average ($81,842) for six days.
Many traders are betting on a rise with borrowed money, so a sharp dip is possible.
watch: Price swings are about as calm as they have been in years and many people are betting on a rise with borrowed money, right as the Fed decides on 28 October with oil-driven worries about a December rate rise. A close back above $81,842 would ease that tension; a slide below $79,000 would turn the week down, and below $76,386 would start a drop signal.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still points up, but the last week has been soft. Short term, the picture is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed below its 50-day average for six days (about 2% under $81,842) and sits about 7% below its 30-day high, while the mood reading is a flat 48 and day-to-day swings are among the calmest in years. A lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, and US Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave in one day, so a quick shake-out is possible. A close above $81,842 (the 50-day average) turns the week clearly up, a close below $79,000 (the bottom of a typical week's swing of about $2,650) turns it down, and in between it stays choppy; the Fed's decision on 28 October is the likely trigger.

Over the next month, the read is mixed. The three-month numbers still look good: price is about 26% above three months ago and roughly three in four of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average, but the last few weeks have faded, with price down about 5% over 30 days. Oil near six-month highs has markets expecting a Fed rate rise in December (KuCoin News, Investing.com), which works against this timeframe. Price must win back $81,842 (the 50-day average) before the month leans up again, with room to climb above $86,603 (the 90-day high); winning back that line would also be the cue to time bigger campaigns.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 10% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about 36% below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a late-stage run; news adds a little here, as Ripple won a US national bank charter and BlackRock is exploring tokenized funds with a Japanese yen stablecoin (both PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,028 (the 200-day average), with $67,439 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. A close back under the 200-day average would weaken this read and argue for slowing spend on new users.

items.theme: Big finance moves deeper into crypto rails
items.why: Ripple said the US banking regulator gave final approval to its national trust bank, which will back its RLUSD stablecoin and offer custody to companies. BlackRock signed a deal with SBI and Startale to explore linking tokenized money-market funds with SBI's yen stablecoin, and Circle has minted about $112B of USDC on Solana this year, nearly double last year.
items.marketing_angle: A trust story for cautious newcomers: well-known banks and fund managers are building on crypto.

items.why: Hyperliquid announced HIP-3*, letting market creators run permissioned markets, and said Kraken's parent Payward plans to be the first US-regulated firm to use it. Separately, the NBA named Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction-market exchanges and signed an agreement with the US CFTC.
items.marketing_angle: An education topic on how on-chain trading venues are becoming regulated, useful for active-trader content.

items.theme: Akash votes to move to Solana
items.why: Akash Network opened a vote to move its network from its own Cosmos chain to Solana, with about 98% of votes in favour so far; voting ends on 2 November and AKT would swap one-for-one. The token is up about 4% in the last day, though the reports do not tie the move to the vote directly.
items.marketing_angle: A simple explainer on what a token migration means for holders would suit existing users.
